chart_data_needs.title: Drone Delivery Unit Cost vs. Ground Delivery (2024-2028)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Can drone delivery achieve cost parity with ground delivery within the planning horizon?
required_metrics: {'year': 2024, 'metric': 'Drone delivery cost per package', 'value': 12.5, 'unit': 'USD', 'entity': 'Industry average (Zipline, Wing)'}
{'year': 2025, 'metric': 'Drone delivery cost per package', 'value': 11.2, 'unit': 'USD', 'entity': 'Industry average (estimated via learning curve)'}
{'year': 2026, 'metric': 'Drone delivery cost per package', 'value': 10.1, 'unit': 'USD', 'entity': 'Industry average (estimated via learning curve)'}
{'year': 2027, 'metric': 'Drone delivery cost per package', 'value': 9.3, 'unit': 'USD', 'entity': 'Industry average (estimated via learning curve)'}
{'year': 2028, 'metric': 'Drone delivery cost per package', 'value': 8.7, 'unit': 'USD', 'entity': 'Industry average (estimated via learning curve)'}
comparison_set: Drone delivery vs. ground delivery cost per package, annual 2024-2028
search_queries: drone delivery cost per package 2024 Zipline Wing
UPS last mile delivery cost per package 2024
FedEx ground delivery cost per package 2024
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use actual reported costs for 2024; for 2025-2028, apply a 10% annual learning curve for drone costs and 2% annual efficiency improvement for ground costs. Mark projected years as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Establishes the cost disadvantage trend and shows whether projected learning curves close the gap.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Management questions whether drone delivery can ever be cost-competitive with traditional last-mile ground delivery.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Drone delivery unit costs remain above $10 per package through 2028, while ground delivery costs stay near $5, making cost parity unlikely without breakthrough technology.

chart_data_needs.title: Consumer Willingness to Pay for Drone Delivery (2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Are consumers willing to pay a premium for drone delivery that covers its higher cost?
search_queries: consumer willingness to pay drone delivery survey 2024
drone delivery premium price consumer survey 2024
McKinsey last mile delivery consumer willingness to pay
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use survey data from nationally representative samples. If multiple surveys exist, use the most recent and cite sample size.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Demonstrates that consumer WTP is below the break-even price, undermining revenue potential.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The business case assumes consumers will pay a premium for speed, but actual WTP data is needed.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Over 70% of consumers are unwilling to pay more than $5 for drone delivery, far below the estimated unit cost of $12.50.

chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use official FAA announcements and company filings. Mark any dates beyond 2024 as estimates based on current guidance.

chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: FAA certification for UAM operations is now expected in 2028, three years later than initial projections, delaying revenue start to 2029.

chart_data_needs.executive_question: Is the total addressable market large enough to support a profitable drone delivery business?

{'year': 2027, 'metric': 'Total drone delivery packages per day', 'value': 80000, 'unit': 'packages/day', 'entity': 'Target city (forecast)'}
{'year': 2028, 'metric': 'Total drone delivery packages per day', 'value': 150000, 'unit': 'packages/day', 'entity': 'Target city (forecast)'}
comparison_set: Annual market size in packages per day
search_queries: urban drone delivery market size forecast 2027
drone delivery packages per day forecast 2028
last mile delivery market size 2024
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use published forecasts from reputable research firms. If only 2024 and 2028 data are available, interpolate using CAGR and mark intermediate years as estimates.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Quantifies the market opportunity and shows that even optimistic forecasts yield insufficient volume for unit cost reduction.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The business case assumes a large and growing market, but actual forecasts need to be examined.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Even the most optimistic forecast shows only 150,000 packages per day by 2028 in our target city, far below the 500,000 needed for breakeven.

chart_data_needs.title: Competitive Landscape: Cost vs. Serviceable Area (2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How does our projected position compare to existing competitors on cost and coverage?
comparison_set: Competitors vs. Project SkyNet on cost and coverage
search_queries: Amazon Prime Air drone delivery cost per package 2024
Wing drone delivery service area 2024
Zipline drone delivery cost per package 2024
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use publicly reported data where available; for competitors that do not disclose, use analyst estimates and note as such.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Shows that competitors already have lower costs and broader coverage, making it difficult for a late entrant to compete.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Management needs to understand the competitive dynamics before committing resources.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Amazon and Wing already achieve lower costs and cover larger serviceable areas, while our projected position is worse on both dimensions.

chart_data_needs.title: Drone Delivery Adoption Funnel: TAM to Realistic Volume (2024)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: What is the realistic daily package volume after accounting for consumer acceptance and regulatory constraints?
search_queries: total packages delivered daily New York City 2024
FAA drone no-fly zones urban areas map
drone delivery adoption rate consumer survey 2024
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use actual data for TAM and regulatory constraints; for adoption and competition, use survey and market share data. Mark any assumptions clearly.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Shows the dramatic reduction from theoretical maximum to achievable volume, highlighting key bottlenecks.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The business case often starts with a large TAM, but real-world constraints reduce it significantly.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: After accounting for regulatory restrictions (70% area loss) and consumer acceptance (50% adoption), realistic volume is only 15% of TAM, or 22,500 packages per day.

chart_data_needs.title: Project SkyNet NPV Sensitivity to Key Variables (2024)

preferred_sources: Internal financial model (based on public data)
Industry benchmarks for cost and revenue

last mile delivery unit economics 2024
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: NPV values are based on internal model assumptions; use public data for input variables where possible. Clearly label as model output.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Identifies the key drivers of NPV and shows that under most scenarios, NPV is negative.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Management needs to understand which assumptions are critical to the business case.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: NPV is most sensitive to unit cost and regulatory delay; even optimistic assumptions yield negative NPV in most scenarios.
